A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MultiGP research work. All 24 pages of v1 and 27 pages of v2, including appendices, support comparison. Equations, tables, and figures can be matched despite relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic and real-world inverse-rendering experiments, component ablations, sampling-distribution analyses, and geometry-robustness results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds global-illumination ablations, texture scores, expanded robustness evaluations, runtime comparisons, and FID/NIQE results.

M1.justification: The texture-extraction cascade, reflectance-map diffusion, scheduling, attention, ControlNet refinement, and losses remain unchanged. Coordinated Guidance becomes Coordinated Scheduling, while new implementation explanations do not establish a procedural change. The material-patch extension in the conclusion is prospective.

E1.justification: The training sources, synthetic datasets, Stanford-ORB, nLMVS, and captured MultiGP dataset remain the same. The GI-off inputs in v2 Tables 1–2 introduce a limited additional lighting condition. Stanford-ORB texture estimation was already evaluated qualitatively in v1, so its new numerical scores do not introduce another task.

E2.justification: v2 Table 6 adds StableNormal-assisted DRM alongside the retained Marigold-assisted DRM comparison, with corresponding MultiGP variants. The principal baseline sets remain intact. IID was already evaluated in v1 Table 5; its additional mean-of-10 row is not a new method.

E3.justification: v2 adds FID/NIQE evaluation, runtime comparisons on one A100 for 1024×1024 inputs, and GI-off controls. The normal-noise sweep extends from a maximum standard deviation of 0.15 to 0.35, corresponding to 25.13° angular error. Existing splits and principal accuracy protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The diagnostic evidence expands substantially: Tables 1–2 test removal of global illumination and extend texture-refinement ablation to illumination and reflectance; Appendix H adds stronger normal corruption and StableNormal-based robustness tests. New Appendix J investigates perceptual-quality differences and includes a visual case of scene-inconsistent DPI details. Existing component, diversity, and fewer-object analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v2 Table 6 adds an IID mean-of-10 summary alongside the retained result under the general top-three-of-ten protocol, introducing an alternative sample aggregation. This does not establish additional runs or seeds. The existing sampling counts and distribution analyses remain unchanged, with no new confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Substantial new results cover real texture accuracy, GI/refinement ablations, robustness, runtime, and perceptual quality. For example, v2 Table 5 reports Stanford-ORB texture RMSE of 0.0255 for MultiGP versus 0.0441 for DPI; Table 8 favors DPI on FID but MultiGP on NIQE. Existing matched accuracy entries remain unchanged. Reported pipeline runtime changes from 28.4 to 25.3 seconds, but v1 does not specify the input resolution, preventing a verified same-setting speedup claim.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, scheduling equations, losses, and Appendix A derivation remain unchanged. Added descriptions of the rendering operator, residual expectation, and model assumptions clarify existing mathematics rather than introducing new definitions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: joint stochastic recovery from a single image with known geometry, four architectural components, complementary information across objects, and ambiguity-aware evaluation. Renaming scheduling and adding supporting experiments do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds discussion of the no-cross-talk limitation and a prospective material-patch extension. It also interprets scheduling and attention as suppressing non-shared global-illumination signals and attributes DPI's FID/NIQE trade-off to hallucinated detail. The existing known-geometry and near-field-lighting limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly specifies rendering and latent resolutions, the 80% triplet probability, object arrangements and rotations, and 50-step single-pass texture refinement. Appendix D identifies the MegaPose variant and perspective rendering. The runtime disclosure and project-access link are updated. These are additional implementation disclosures, without evidence that the underlying training procedure changed.

R1.justification: v2 adds the StableNormal citation and its experimental role. Appendix J further positions MultiGP against DPI's panorama prior, while related work adds regression-to-the-mean as an explanation for smooth predictions. The broader research positioning remains intact; reference renumbering and access-date additions are bibliographic edits.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording and typo corrections, changes scheduling terminology, expands explanatory passages, renames Appendix B to include inference, and adds Appendix J. The main narrative and section organization remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds training examples in Figure 9, a DPI comparison in Figure 16, and new Tables 5 and 8. Several existing tables gain rows, and retained figures and tables move or receive new numbers. These are localized display additions and layout adjustments rather than a document-wide visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The added GI controls, stronger geometry tests, and concrete training/inference details improve scrutiny of the method's physical assumptions and reproducibility. New texture and runtime comparisons also strengthen the supporting evidence. The gains are limited by noisy texture pseudo-ground-truth and Appendix J's inference of scene-specific hallucination from FID/NIQE, which those metrics alone do not establish. Overall, v2 modestly strengthens the existing paper without changing its core method or established benchmark results.
